Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 1 Purpose of the policy
Pulse believes that every employee, including the employee who is leaving the company, is treated with respect and dignity. This policy lays down standard and transparent procedures to ensure smooth exit of the employee from the company.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 2 Scope of the policy
This policy is applicable to all employees, probationers and trainees working at Corporate, Depot, R&D, Field and Factory of the Pulse Group.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 3 Separation due to voluntary resignation
3.1 Employee desiring to leave the company, needs to submit a resignation letter in HRMS, stating the reason for leaving to the reporting manager.

3.2 Upon receipt of employee's resignation, the reporting manager, should have a detailed discussion with the employee and the HOD, and provide necessary recommendations regarding resignation acceptance or employee retention to the HR department within 48 hours from receipt of employee's resignation.

3.3 It is mandatory for all the employees to serve the notice period as mentioned in their appointment letters to allow a reasonable amount of time to transfer ongoing workloads.

3.4 Leaves during the notice period will be applicable as per the Leave and Attendance policy of the company.

3.5 Early relieving, waiver of the notice period may be considered only for critical cases recommended by the HOD and will be subject to approval from Head HR and the Management.

3.6 Employee has to full-fill all the duties and obligations assigned to him/her during the notice period and has to ensure full co-operation in handing over charge of the work being handled.

3.7 The notice period will be extended as decided by the HOD and HR in the event of non-cooperation from the employee and may also attract necessary disciplinary action if required.

3.8 The HR department will coordinate the employee's no due clearance and FFS process as laid down in this policy.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 4 Separation due to non-performance
4.1. As a part of the performance management process, employees whose performance is below the required standards will be put on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) as laid down in the Performance Management Policy of the company.

4.1 Reporting Manager, HOD and HR will review the PIP, conduct a detailed appraisal discussion with the employee and if there is no improvement, as a last resort, the employee will be put under the exit process.

4.2 It is mandatory for the employees to serve their notice period.

4.3 HR department will coordinate the employee's no due clearance and FFS process as laid down in this policy.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 5 Separation due to Superannuation/retirement
5.1. As per the appointment letter/employment contract letter the retirement of an employee will be on attaining the age of 58.

5.2. The retirement date shall be calculated on the basis of their date of birth mentioned in their 10th marks certificate submitted by the employee while joining the company.

5.3. HR will inform the employee, reporting manager and the HOD about the employees' retirement date at least 4 months in advance in order to plan the workload.

5.4. HR department will coordinate the employee's no due clearance and FFS process as laid down in this policy.

5.5. As per the business need and mutual agreement, the Management may consider re- appointment with the company as a Consultant for a fixed term period and as per the terms of the agreement.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 6 Exit Interview
6.1. HR will conduct the exit interview of the employees at the following intervals.

6.1.1. One - within 2 working days from receipt of communication regarding employee's resignation using Exit Interview Form A (Annexure 1).

6.1.1.1. HR to conduct one-one discussion with the employee referring to the questions in the form.

6.1.1.2. HR shall take necessary comments on the form.

6.1.2. Two - during the last week of the employee leaving the service using Exit Interview Form B (Annexure 2).

6.1.2.1. Employee shall fill the form and HR shall conduct one-one discussion with the employee.

6.1.2.2. HR shall take necessary comments on the form.

6.2. The intention of exit interviews should be to understand the actual reasons for leaving, improvement areas and positive things about his/her work.

6.3. Discussion shall be conducted in a constructive and professional manner and inappropriate questions that will discriminate or humiliate candidate's abilities or personality must be avoided.

6.4. The feedback received should be shared with the reporting manager and the HOD and further with the Management for further retention & improvement initiatives at workplace.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 7 No Dues Procedure
7.1. HR will initiate No Dues Clearance Form (Annexure 3) in HRMS to the employees on or before 2 days before the last working day for getting clearances from all the departments and then shall submit the form to HR for processing the full and final settlement.

7.2. Employee has to return ID card, Keys, Access Cards, laptop, mobile, credit card, vehicle and any other company assets as applicable to the concerned departments for their clearance, and submit the No dues clearance form to the HR within 7 days from the issuance date.

7.3. Failure to return any item will result in necessary deductions from the employee's FFS.

7.4. Wherever mandated by the company, the employee has to sign the confidentiality agreement document with the company.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 8 Full and Final Settlement (FFS)
8.1. HR shall close the FFS within 30 days from the receipt of the No Due Clearance Form from the employee.

8.2. HR will coordinate with Finance team and process the no due form considering all dues and payment to the employees like final salary payments, notice period recovery, gratuity, outstanding leaves, salary advances and any other financial obligations.

8.3. HR will communicate the settlement amount or recovery amount to the employee after receiving the FFS from the Finance department.

8.4. Employee has to revert to HR within 48 hours from the receipt of FFS for any clarifications or consent otherwise.

8.5. Failure to respond within the specified time will be considered as an acceptance from the employee.

8.6. Upon acceptance, HR shall advise the Finance to process the FSS and the amount will be credited to the bank account of the employee within 7 working days thereafter.

8.7. The last month salary will be paid along with the FFS.

8.8. HR shall issue Relieving and Experience Letter (Annexure 4) to the employees after the FFS clearance.

8.9. In case of recovery, the Relieving and Experience letter will be issued to the employee only after the dues are recovered from the employee and after the FFS is processed by HR and cleared by Finance.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 9 Dismissal on Disciplinary grounds
9.1. Termination on account of breach of conduct, violation of established rules, procedures, integrity, values or ethics, un-authorized absence, repeated absence, tardiness will be governed by the rules of code of conduct.

9.2. An enquiry will be conducted by the disciplinary committee wherein the employee may be asked to appear for an enquiry so as to provide him/her an opportunity for being heard.

9.3. If found guilty for breaching the conduct and where the management has lost confidence and trust on the employee, he/she will be dismissed from the company by giving adequate reasons and with or without notice pay at Management's discretion.

9.4. Full & Final settlement will be done within 7 working days from FFS clearance.

9.5. Employee will be issued a Termination Letter (Annexure 4) with immediate effect.

9.6. No Relieving and Experience Letter will be issued to employees dismissed on disciplinary grounds.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 10 Administration
HR department will administer this policy.

Policy: Pulse Seperation Policy (Version V.01, effective 2026-01-01)
Policy ID: pulse_seperation_policy
Section: 11 Exceptions
Any exceptions to the policy shall be approved by Head HR.

The Management reserves its right to amend the policy as per the business need and if appropriate at any time. Such amended policy will be communicated to the employees through the appropriate channel.
